summary: Bradford's Instagram record on housing centers on increasing supply, reducing what he describes as government-imposed costs, and streamlining approvals. Bradford repeatedly supports "missing middle" housing, multiplexes, sixplexes, mid-rise on Avenues, garden and laneway suites, modular and rapid-build construction, office-to-residential conversions, and ending exclusionary zoning. Bradford supports purpose-built rental and supportive housing with wraparound services, citing East York projects he advanced. Bradford opposes additional housing-related taxes, including the Vacant Home Tax in its current form and a luxury home tax, and characterizes Mayor Chow's rental incentive and public-builder approaches as inadequate. Bradford has moved motions to cut development charges (25% on condos, 100% on purpose-built rental), expand the first-time homebuyer rebate, raise the Avenues unit cap from 30 to 60, and streamline modular permitting. Bradford frames red tape, fees, and design rules (e.g., angular plane) as central barriers.
